Steps: 1) Open the tenant sign-in page; 2) Enter the evaluator email and permanent password; 3) Submit the sign-in form; 4) Observe the first surface
Expected Result: Sign-in is accepted and the app shows either the face gate (Register your face / Verify your face) or the Evaluation desk; no other role workspace renders
Test Data: Evaluator email + permanent password resolved from .env; tenant URL from WEB_APP_URL
Notes: tests/web/testcases/evaluator.spec.ts EVL-01 via signInRole('evaluator'); both post-login surfaces are documented valid states (utils/liveEvaluation.ts openEvaluatorWorkspace).

Expected Result: The permanent password is accepted, the temporary password is no longer usable, and the face gate or desk renders
Test Data: Synthetic permanent password supplied by the run environment; temporary password never stored
Notes: utils/dvsAuth.ts resolves state 'password-set'; SetPasswordPage drives the form. Prompt section 16.1 step 1.

Title: Evaluator sidebar exposes only the Evaluation desk

Steps: 1) Inspect the Primary navigation complementary region; 2) List every module button; 3) Compare with the Admin and Chief module sets

Notes: evaluator.spec.ts EVL-02 asserts the foreign modules have count 0. Prompt section 19 + section 21 sidebar inventory.

Notes: evaluator.spec.ts EVL-03.

Title: Desk workflow guide lists the five documented stages in order

Title: Evaluator guidance dialog is dismissible and does not block EVALUATE

Title: First entry shows the Register your face prompt with an Open camera control

Title: Human completes enrollment and the app reports a verified face
Preconditions: Enrollment dialog open with a live camera

Title: Enrollment is one-time and later sign-ins only request a quick face check
Preconditions: Enrollment completed in an earlier session
Steps: 1) Sign out; 2) Sign in again as the same evaluator; 3) Observe the face surface offered

Title: Re-running Enroll on an already enrolled evaluator does not create a second enrollment
Preconditions: Evaluator already enrolled in this tenant
Steps: 1) Reach the face surface; 2) If an Enroll control is offered, run the enrollment again; 3) Read the face status endpoint and the enrollment records

Title: Denying the camera blocks the secure evaluation flow with a clear message
Preconditions: Browser camera permission denied for the tenant origin
Steps: 1) Sign in as an unenrolled evaluator; 2) Open the camera dialog; 3) Deny the browser camera prompt; 4) Attempt to continue to the desk and to EVALUATE
Expected Result: The flow is blocked with an explicit camera message; the desk or secure check never reaches a state where marking is possible
Notes: docs/testcases/05-evaluator.md EVL-15; prompt section 16.2 step 6 forbids bypassing the camera check.

Title: A second face in frame fails the Single face check
Preconditions: Enrollment or verification dialog open with a live camera
Steps: 1) Open the camera; 2) Place two faces in frame; 3) Observe the Single face check and the Enroll/Verify control
Expected Result: Single face reports a failure and Enroll/Verify stays unavailable until one face is present
Test Data: Live camera with two people in frame
Notes: Single face is a documented check (prompt section 16.2 step 3); the failure text must be captured live.

Title: Camera loss during enrollment leaves no partial enrollment and offers recovery
Preconditions: Enrollment dialog open with the camera streaming
Steps: 1) Start the checks; 2) Physically disconnect or disable the camera mid-capture; 3) Reconnect; 4) Retry enrollment
Expected Result: The app reports the failed camera check, does not report success, records no enrolled state, and a retry succeeds once the camera returns

Notes: Related to docs/testcases/05-evaluator.md EVL-15/24; the mid-capture recovery surface must be observed live.

Title: Face enrollment dialog is fully operable from the keyboard
Preconditions: Enrollment dialog rendered with the camera streaming
Steps: 1) Reach the dialog with Tab only; 2) Move between checks and the camera/Enroll controls; 3) Activate Enroll with Enter or Space; 4) Attempt to Tab out of the dialog
Expected Result: Focus reaches every control, Enroll activates from the keyboard, focus does not escape behind the modal, and each check state is announced
Notes: No accessibility assertions exist in the repo; capture focus order and announcements in the live tenant before automating.

Title: Enrollment cannot succeed without a live camera capture
Preconditions: Unenrolled evaluator; camera blocked or replaced with a still-image device
Steps: 1) Open the enrollment dialog; 2) Block the camera or select a still image as the media device; 3) Attempt Enroll; 4) POST /api/v1/evaluator-management/face/login directly; 5) Read the face status
Expected Result: No path establishes an enrolled state without a live capture; the direct API call is refused and face status stays enrolled = false
Notes: Prompt section 16.2 step 7 forbids bypassing camera/face checks; the server-side refusal shape for the direct call must be observed live.

Title: Face status endpoint agrees with the enrollment state shown in the UI

Title: Secure evaluation check dialog lists the five policy rows

Preconditions: Workspace open in a 1366x768 viewport
Steps: 1) Resize to 1366x768; 2) Scroll the marks table and the viewer; 3) Locate Submit evaluation, Pause evaluation and Grand Total
Expected Result: All marking inputs, Grand Total and the workflow actions are reachable without horizontal clipping or overlapping overlays
Notes: Responsive behaviour is not covered in the repo; capture the real layout before asserting.

Title: Repeated pause and resume cycles keep the session and marks stable
Preconditions: Workspace open with marks entered
Steps: 1) Pause and resume five times through the full chain; 2) Re-read marks, totals and the timer
Expected Result: Every cycle restores the same workspace state, marks and totals are unchanged, and no duplicate draft events accumulate
Notes: Not covered in the repo; verify that drafts are not duplicated per resume.

Title: The marking flow is completable with the keyboard only
Preconditions: Workspace open on a 24-question script
Steps: 1) Tab to Marks for 1; 2) Type a mark and Tab to the next field; 3) Continue to Grand Total and Submit evaluation; 4) Note any focus trap
Expected Result: Every mark field, the totals and the submit control are reachable in a sensible order, focus is never trapped or lost, and all marks can be entered without a mouse
Notes: No keyboard/a11y assertions exist in the repo; EvaluationDeskPage only relies on labelled inputs.

Title: The secure check dialog traps focus and returns it to EVALUATE on close
Preconditions: Secure evaluation check dialog open
Steps: 1) Open the dialog from EVALUATE; 2) Tab repeatedly to check focus stays inside; 3) Close the dialog and read the focused element
Expected Result: Focus cycles inside the modal while open and returns to the EVALUATE control when it closes
Notes: Modal focus management is not asserted anywhere; verify on the live tenant.

Title: Every marks input is addressable by its accessible label
Preconditions: Workspace open
Steps: 1) Enumerate the marks inputs by accessible name; 2) Compare with the question numbers in the consolidated table
Expected Result: Each mark field exposes the label Marks for {n} matching its question, with no duplicate or missing labels
Notes: EvaluationDeskPage.marksInput uses getByLabel(/^Marks for {n}\b/), which requires the accessible label.

Title: Marks inputs expose the per-question maximum to assistive tech
Preconditions: Workspace open
Steps: 1) Inspect the marks input attributes for each section; 2) Compare the exposed maximum with the section maxima
Expected Result: Each input exposes a numeric constraint (max or described limit) equal to the question maximum, so screen-reader users are told the range
Notes: Out-of-range rejection is verified, but the client-side constraint attributes were not captured.

Title: Blocking mark errors are exposed as an alert dialog for assistive tech
Preconditions: Workspace open; an invalid mark entered
Steps: 1) Enter -8 or 99 on a question; 2) Blur; 3) Inspect the dialog role and name
Expected Result: The blocking error is announced as an alertdialog with the app's own message, so a screen reader user hears the rejection
Test Data: Dialog role alertdialog; name Evaluation alert
Notes: EvaluationDeskPage.submitEvaluation queries getByRole('alertdialog', {name:'Evaluation alert'}).

Title: The exit reason group is operable without a mouse
Preconditions: Exit this script? dialog open
Steps: 1) Tab into the Reason for exiting group; 2) Select a reason with arrow keys or Space; 3) Confirm Save and exit with Enter
Expected Result: All seven reasons are reachable and selectable from the keyboard and the exit records the selected reason
Notes: Reason options are documented but their widget type and keyboard behaviour were not captured.

Title: The script viewer is keyboard operable
Preconditions: Workspace open
Steps: 1) Tab to Previous page, Go to page and Next page; 2) Page forward with the keyboard; 3) Read the page indicator
Expected Result: Each viewer control is reachable and activatable from the keyboard and the page indicator updates after each change
Test Data: Controls Previous page, Go to page, Next page
Notes: EvaluationDeskPage drives these controls with clicks only; keyboard operability is unverified.

Title: Zoom and theme controls are keyboard reachable and announce their state
Preconditions: Workspace open
Steps: 1) Tab to Zoom out, the zoom percentage, Zoom in and Theme: auto; 2) Change the zoom from the keyboard; 3) Read the announced percentage
Expected Result: Controls are reachable and the current zoom percentage and theme are exposed as text or values
Test Data: Controls Zoom out, Zoom in, Fit to width, Theme: auto
Notes: Labels are verified from prompt section 21; accessibility state exposure is not captured.

Title: Saved and unsaved marks are visually distinguishable
Preconditions: Workspace open with some marks saved and one just typed
Steps: 1) Type a mark and read the field/save state; 2) Blur and re-read; 3) Read the totals
Expected Result: The app distinguishes a pending value from a saved value (indicator, styling or message) so the evaluator knows what is stored
Test Data: One pending mark and one saved mark
Notes: EvaluationDeskPage relies on a 150 ms pause after blur, which suggests an async save state that needs explicit UI evidence.

Title: The invalid-mark message identifies the question and the allowed range
Preconditions: Workspace open; an out-of-range mark entered
Steps: 1) Enter 11 on question 21; 2) Blur; 3) Read the acknowledgement dialog
Expected Result: The dialog names the question and the permitted maximum so the evaluator can correct the entry
Notes: The rejection is documented with an OK dialog but the message text was not captured.

Title: SOS Help and Remarks are reachable and do not disturb marks
Preconditions: Workspace open with marks entered
Steps: 1) Open SOS Help; 2) Dismiss it; 3) Open Remarks and add a note; 4) Re-read the marks
Expected Result: Both surfaces open and close without losing the workspace state, and marks and totals are unchanged
Notes: Labels are verified from prompt section 21; behaviour is not covered in the repo.

Title: The desk workflow guide shows the current stage and the next action
Preconditions: Evaluator on the desk with one submitted and one pending script
Steps: 1) Read the workflow guide; 2) Compare the highlighted stage with the actual state; 3) Note the next action offered
Expected Result: The highlighted stage matches the evaluator's state and the next action (for example Send your report) is reachable from the guide
Test Data: One submitted script plus one pending script
Notes: Prompt section 16.1 step 2 documents the guide; stage highlighting behaviour was not captured.

Title: Submitted evaluation row is stored exactly once
Preconditions: Evaluation submitted after the timer ended.
Steps: 1) Query the evaluation and work item rows; 2) Compare status and timestamps.
Expected Result: One submitted evaluation row with submit and timer timestamps; no duplicate submission row.
Notes: Read-only query; submission idempotency is also asserted at the API layer.

Title: Marks rows match the workspace totals
Preconditions: Every question marked and submitted.
Steps: 1) Query marks for the evaluation and round; 2) Sum them and compare with Grand Total.
Expected Result: One mark row per question and round; the sum equals the workspace total and Final Marks.
Notes: Include zero-mark and unanswered rows.

Title: Draft marks persist and are replaced on submit
Preconditions: Marks saved, script exited, then submitted.
Steps: 1) Query draft rows after save-and-exit; 2) Query again after submit.
Expected Result: Draft values match the saved input; submit promotes them without duplicate rows or lost marks.
Notes: No data loss across pause, exit and resume.

Title: Face enrollment row is single per user
Preconditions: Evaluator completed face enrollment.
Steps: 1) Query the enrollment row by user; 2) Repeat the face check.
Expected Result: Exactly one enrolled row per user with the expected status and timestamp; a repeat check does not insert a second enrollment.
Notes: Never store or log biometric media.

Title: 100 evaluators submit at the same time
Preconditions: 100 disposed evaluator assignments with submitted marks.
Steps: 1) Submit all evaluations in parallel; 2) Re-read each evaluation and count rows.
Expected Result: Each evaluation is submitted once; no duplicate rows, lost marks or 5xx.
Notes: Record the measured p95 and confirm the agreed budget in Notes before gating CI.

Title: Twenty-four autosaves in ten seconds lose no mark
Preconditions: An open workspace with a 24-question script.
Steps: 1) Save every mark in a rapid burst; 2) Re-read the workspace and database.
Expected Result: Every save is acknowledged; final values and totals match; no version conflict or lost update.
Notes: Record the measured p95 and confirm the agreed budget in Notes before gating CI.

Title: Ten times script volume keeps the workspace responsive
Preconditions: 10x the normal script/question volume.
Steps: 1) Open and page through the script; 2) Measure workspace load and total accuracy.
Expected Result: p95 within the agreed budget; all pages and totals are exact.
